messages:
Nora (Sales): Heads-up — Polaris legal wants final security Qs answered and their infra team is hitting intermittent TTFT regressions during a POC run. Can we swarm?
Chen (Polaris): Confirm. POC load: bursts of ~40 parallel chat sessions. Avg prompt 90 tokens, reply ~80 tokens. Region: eu-central-1. Symptoms: spikes to 1.4s first-byte, occasional 503 and socket reset logs.
Omar (SE): Thanks @Nora @Chen. Quick triage questions: which deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)? model variant and are you using streaming? Also paste one request_id from the 503 window.
Chen (Polaris): We're on a Dedicated trial instance (ded-pt-003) using rwinf-redwood-33b-v1, streaming=true. Sample request: req_20260502_a9c3.
Rhea (Eng-SRE): Pulling logs for req_20260502_a9c3 — seeing upstream connection resets and elevated egress latency to the customer VPC peering endpoint. Snippet: 
"[2026-05-02T11:42:07Z] req=req_20260502_a9c3 first_byte_ms=1423 exec_ms=220 client_err=connection_reset egress_ms=540 batch_size=32"
That egress_ms is large and correlates with 503s. Any NAT gateway retries?
Chen (Polaris): We're on private subnet with a managed NAT; we did see AWS NAT metrics spike.
Omar (SE): Two parallel fixes: (1) short-term — reduce batch size and enable prefix cache warmup to cut queue latency and exec path; (2) medium-term — change routing to use an internal VPC peering path or increase NAT capacity. Try this overlay in the POC config: 
```yaml
batching:
  max_batch_size: 12
  min_batch_timeout_ms: 3
cache:
  prefix_cache: true
  prefix_ttl_ms: 300000
warmup:
  warmup_requests: 50
routing_policy:
  prefer_local_network: true
```
Apply via Console -> Dedicated -> Instance -> "POC Overrides".
Chen (Polaris): Will apply now. Any quick command to measure first-byte distribution?
Omar (SE): Run this in your env: 
```bash
for i in {1..40}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwinf-redwood-33b-v1","input":"<sample>","stream":false}' \
    https://dedicated.eu-central-1.redwood.com/v1/generate | jq '.timing.first_byte_ms'; \
done | sort -n | awk 'NR==int(NR*0.5){print "p50:"$0} NR==int(NR*0.95){print "p95:"$0} END{print "done"}'
```
Rhea (Eng-SRE): Also check your NAT gateway CloudWatch metrics for "ActiveConnections" and "ErrorPortAllocation" around the incidents. If NAT throttling shows up, add an extra NAT or switch to NAT Gateway Auto Scaling (or VPC Egress via Transit Gateway).
infra-bot: Alert: ded-pt-003 observed NATGateway: HighPortUsage at 2026-05-02T11:40:00Z
Chen (Polaris): Overlay applied. Running the non-streaming 40-run now — initial run: p50=320ms p95=610ms p99=980ms. No 503s in this short window.
Omar (SE): Good. Two notes: streaming=true adds extra first-byte due to chunked handshake; for true TTFT compare stream=false. Also batch_size 32 earlier shows queue_ms ~480 in our logs; lowering batch size reduced queue wait.
Sasha (Security): For the questionnaire: short bullets for legal — Dedicated trial runs in customer VPC with optional Private control plane, we support Customer-Managed KMS, SOC2 Type II, ISO27001, and can redact PII in logs on ingest. I'll attach a boilerplate answer set.
Ben (AE): Commercial note: Dedicated POC includes trial reserved capacity; if Polaris needs consistent sub-400ms p50 at their concurrency we should discuss an uplift and reserved worker add-on. I can prepare pricing options.
Chen (Polaris): Curious about prefix_ttl_ms — we saw misses earlier. How long before cache heat?
Rhea (Eng-SRE): TTL controls how long prefix entries are kept; with chat work you want a longer TTL (we set 5min above) during POC. Also run a short warmup against representative prefixes: 50 distinct warmup requests should populate the KV cache for most flows.
Omar (SE): If exec_ms remains high after cache warmup, consider model variant rwinf-redwood-33b-4bit which reduces exec path by ~30-40% exec time. We'll run a 15-prompt quality check if you want.
Chen (Polaris): Please run the quality check — financial/legal semantics matter for us.
Omar (SE): Will run 15 evals vs 33b and 33b-4bit; report by EOD.
Nora (Sales): Action items: @Omar run quality evals (owner Omar) — EOD. @Rhea check NAT metrics and recommend infra steps (owner Rhea) — 2h. @Sasha post Q&A boilerplate for legal (owner Sasha). @Ben prepare pricing uplift scenarios for dedicated workers (owner Ben) — EOD. @Chen re-run full 40-concurrency test and post p50/p95/p99 when done.
Chen (Polaris): Re-ran after warmup + overlay, streaming=false: p50=280ms p95=540ms p99=900ms, no socket resets in 15m window. Streaming=true still shows ~360ms p50.
Rhea (Eng-SRE): NAT metrics show port exhaustion spikes. Immediate recommended fix: add another NAT gateway or move to an Elastic Fabric NAT mode. We'll open infra ticket with Polaris' cloud admin.
Sasha (Security): Posted the boilerplate to the thread and attached a short dataflow diagram.
Ben (AE): I'll draft pricing options: (A) keep Hosted with burst workers, (B) Dedicated + extra worker pool (est +2.2x cost), (C) Private deploy. Sending note by EOD.
Omar (SE): If anything reappears, tag this thread and we'll re-open the POC overlay or spin extra workers temporarily. Keep sample prompts and the 40-run logs attached.
Chen (Polaris): Thanks team, huge help. I'll push the logs and legal questions into the shared drive and loop back.
Nora (Sales): Closing the swarm for now. Will consolidate outcomes for legal and next commercial steps.
(END)
